defaults.permitted_development: In Wales, an internal garage conversion will not usually need planning permission if the building is not enlarged and the outside is not materially altered, but a separate dwelling, estate-condition issue or wider enlargement can change that answer.

rules.height_rules: If the work stays inside the existing garage shell there is no new householder height allowance to use. Any upward extension, raised roof or rebuilt garage would need to be assessed separately.
rules.depth_rules: A purely internal conversion is the simplest case. If the proposal extends the garage, adds a link, projects outward or enlarges the footprint, the normal extension rules or a planning application come into play.
rules.boundary_rules: Check whether the garage was required for parking by an earlier permission and whether any frontage, highway or neighbour-facing changes need a closer planning review. Article 4 directions and estate conditions can also remove the simpler route.
rules.roof_rules: If the conversion also alters the roof, separate Wales roof alteration rules apply. A simple internal fit-out does not itself create a new roof allowance.
rules.materials_rules: Any infill where the garage door is removed should sit comfortably with the dwelling and look intentional rather than patched in. Listed building or conservation controls can still override the ordinary route.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales, an internal garage conversion will not usually need planning permission if the building is not enlarged and the outside is not materially altered, but a separate dwelling, estate-condition issue or wider enlargement can change that answer.

restrictions.conservation_area: In Wales, conservation area controls and any Article 4 direction can remove normal householder permitted development rights for visible external work. Check the planning register before relying on national allowances.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may be needed for internal or external works that affect the character of a listed building or its curtilage structures. Minor-looking changes can still need consent in Wales.
restrictions.article4_notes: No borough-wide Article 4 note is recorded here, but site-specific directions or planning conditions can still remove permitted development rights on particular properties.

rules.permitted_development: Planning permission is not usually required in Wales for a simple internal garage conversion, but enlarging the structure, making stronger external changes or creating an independent dwelling can move it outside the ordinary householder route.

rules.height_rules: Garage conversion does not create a fresh height allowance in Wales. The moment the scheme raises the roof, adds an upper floor or materially rebuilds the structure, it stops being a simple internal conversion.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is not the main garage-conversion test in Wales. Keeping the work inside the existing shell is usually easiest; once the building projects outward or grows, use the normal extension framework instead.
rules.boundary_rules: The key local checks are often parking retention, estate conditions and frontage design. Even a simple garage-door infill can become a planning issue where the altered elevation is prominent or the original approval protected garage parking.
rules.roof_rules: Garage conversion on its own does not open a separate roof right. Any proposal to lift, rebuild or materially alter the garage roof should be treated as external development in its own right.
rules.materials_rules: When a garage door is replaced, aim for brickwork, openings and detailing that belong with the rest of the dwelling. Front-elevation changes are usually what attract the closest design scrutiny.

restrictions.article4_notes: No borough-wide Article 4 note is recorded here, but site-specific directions or planning conditions can still remove permitted development rights on particular properties.

rules.permitted_development: A straightforward internal garage conversion is usually the lowest-risk route in Wales. The position changes if the garage is enlarged, the external appearance is materially altered or the space is intended to operate as separate living accommodation.

rules.height_rules: A pure garage conversion works within the existing envelope, so there is no separate conversion height right. Once the roofline is lifted or the garage is rebuilt, treat that element as external development in its own right.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate garage-conversion depth right in Wales. Staying within the existing footprint is the low-risk route, whereas any outward projection or linked enlargement has to be considered under extension rules or a full planning route.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary and frontage issues usually come from the external alterations rather than the internal fit-out. Also check whether an earlier permission required the garage or parking arrangement to be retained as part of the approved layout.
rules.roof_rules: Roof changes are not part of the ordinary internal conversion question. Once the scheme includes a raised roof, dormer or other visible roof alteration, assess that work separately under the normal Welsh rules.
rules.materials_rules: The external treatment of a former garage opening matters more than the internal fit-out. A well-matched infill wall, window or doorway usually reads best on the house.
